subject: ventures/cbam-cost-estimator
professional: a customs / CBAM compliance consultant who prepares authorised-declarant applications and annual CBAM declarations for EU importers of steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers and hydrogen

evidence.correctness: Wrote an independent Python model (scratchpad/cbam/ind.py) from Regulation 2023/956 Art 21/22/31 and the ETS Directive Art 10a(1a) phase-out (free allocation remaining 97.5, 95, 90, 77.5, 51.5, 39, 26.5, 14, 0%), not from calc.mjs. The certificate arithmetic matches compute() exactly: 1,000 t steel at 2.0/1.37, 2026, EUR 80 -> 664.25 certificates, EUR 53,140; a 2030 aluminium + clinker mix with EUR 10 paid abroad -> 3,914.733 certificates, EUR 313,178.64; 2034 ladder EUR 160,000. CBAM_FACTOR equals the Art 10a(1a) schedule. But four outputs a user acts on are wrong: (1) hydrogen-only imports (10 t) report 'under the 50 t threshold, so you are likely outside CBAM obligations' although Regulation 2025/2083 excludes hydrogen and electricity from the de minimis exemption, so every hydrogen import is in scope; (2) exactly 50 t reports 'over the 50 t threshold' though the exemption covers mass that does not exceed 50 t; (3) fertilisers with Commission default values get the 10/20/30% mark-up where Implementing Regulation 2025/2621 sets 1% for fertilisers (300 t ammonia 2028 at EUR 70: EUR 35,847 vs 21,231, 69% over); (4) tonnes typed '1,200' parse as 1.2 t and flip the threshold verdict to 'outside CBAM'.
evidence.completeness: Every feature the README and page list runs end to end on node: certificates, euro cost, cost per tonne, % of goods value, 50 t flag, 2026-2034 ladder, 50-150% price ladder, origin carbon price deduction, default-value mark-up, summary text and CSV download (sample test passes). The page's 'Not decided' list discloses CN coverage, precursors, indirect emissions, electricity and declarant deadlines. No stubs or dead links; served page https://marisstella.app/cbam-cost-estimator/ returns 200. The features are present; their domain errors are scored under correctness and domain.
evidence.verification: Ran cd ventures/cbam-cost-estimator && node --test '*.test.mjs': 26 pass, 0 fail. Seeded 6 mutations in calc.mjs, each reverted with git checkout (git diff --stat -- ventures/ clean afterwards): removing the hydrogen filter (84) and removing the origin-deduction cap (93) were caught; threshold < -> <= (85), CBAM factor 2030 0.485 -> 0.5 (9), mark-up after 2027 0.30 -> 0.20 (16), and the year ladder using the selected year's factor instead of each year's (109) all survived. 4 of 6 survived: tests pin only 2026 and 2034 factors, check ladder monotonicity rather than values, and one test asserts the wrong hydrogen rule.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (163 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, index.html. Pure functions, one validate path, clear formula comments. Defects: num() replaces only the first comma with a dot, so '1,200' becomes 1.2 and '1.200,5' is rejected; the ladder re-implements the per-line cost loop instead of reusing it; dates.quarterlyHolding is guarded by year >= 2026, always true; an exempt importer still sees 'Estimated CBAM cost for 2026: EUR 1,288.32' headline (20 t steel) next to the 'likely outside CBAM' finding; the hydrogen 'mass' shows as 'Total mass 0 t'.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer, not-advice clause, 'Everything runs in your browser' and illustrative-preset labels are present and asserted by page.test.mjs; no network calls in index.html or calc.mjs (grep). Dates on the page match the Omnibus as reported by secondary sources: certificate sales from 1 February 2027, declaration and surrender by 30 September of the next year, 50% quarterly holding from 2027. Two claims are not backed by the code: the page promises 'whether you are under the 50-tonne threshold' and gets it wrong for hydrogen and at exactly 50 t; the defaults option says it 'adds the mark-up' but applies the steel/aluminium mark-up to fertilisers. llms.txt source links the github.io host, but the served llms.txt links marisstella.app (curl), so that is source-only, not counted.
evidence.fitness: An importer finance lead can type tonnes and supplier intensities and get an order-of-magnitude cost and ramp in two minutes, which is the job the page states. A CBAM consultant could not hand it to a client as is: a hydrogen importer is told they are probably exempt, a fertiliser importer on default values sees a cost about 30% too high in 2028, there are no CN codes, no precursor emissions, no Commission default values by country, and the free-allocation benchmarks are not the CBAM benchmarks the definitive period uses.
evidence.domain: Method (embedded emissions x (1 + mark-up) minus benchmark x remaining free allocation, times price, less origin carbon price) is the Art 21/22/31 shape and the phase-out table is right. Departures: hydrogen de minimis rule inverted; threshold boundary (does not exceed 50 t) off by one; fertiliser mark-up 1% (2025/2621) not modelled; benchmark presets mix vintages: steel 1.328, EAF 0.283, aluminium 1.514, clinker 0.766, ammonia 1.619, nitric 0.302 are the 2013-2020 ETS product benchmarks (Decision 2011/278), hydrogen 6.84 is the 2021-2025 value, and none is the definitive-period CBAM benchmark from the December 2025 implementing act; the origin deduction applies the foreign price to certificates rather than to the emissions actually priced abroad net of rebates (disclosed as an approximation). Sources: Regulation 2023/956 and 2025/2083 as summarised by PwC, EY, Mayer Brown and Clifford Chance (web search 2026-11-12), 2025/2621 mark-ups from secondary guides; the Official Journal text was not fetched, and benchmark values are cited from the auditor's knowledge of the ETS benchmark decisions.

Default-value mark-up 10/20/30% is applied to fertilisers; Implementing Regulation 2025/2621 sets 1% for fertilisers, so a fertiliser importer on defaults sees cost up to about 30% too high (EUR 35,847 vs 21,231 in the 2028 ammonia case)
num() replaces only the first comma with a dot, so '1,200' tonnes becomes 1.2 t (flipping the threshold verdict) and '1.200,5' is rejected

Benchmark presets mix 2013-2020 ETS benchmarks (steel 1.328, aluminium 1.514, clinker 0.766, ammonia 1.619) with a 2021-2025 one (hydrogen 6.84), uncited, and none is the definitive-period CBAM benchmark; presets understate certificates if left in
Exactly 50 t is reported as over the threshold; the exemption covers mass that does not exceed 50 t ('Total mass 50 t is over the 50 t')
4 of 6 seeded mutations survive: tests pin only the 2026 and 2034 factors, check the year ladder for monotonicity not values, and never test the post-2027 mark-up or the threshold boundary
An importer under the threshold still gets a non-zero 'Estimated CBAM cost' headline; quarterlyHolding is guarded by year >= 2026, always true

verdict: CBAM Cost Estimator does the certificate arithmetic right: two independent cases match to the cent and the 2026-2034 phase-out table equals the ETS Directive schedule. It does not meet the bar. A CBAM consultant checking the 2026 rules would find that a hydrogen importer is told they are probably exempt (the 50 t exemption excludes hydrogen, it does not exempt it), exactly 50 t is called over the threshold, fertilisers on default values get the 10/20/30% mark-up instead of 1%, and '1,200' tonnes reads as 1.2 t. The benchmark presets are a mix of stale ETS vintages. 26 tests pass but 4 of 6 seeded mutations survive, and one test asserts the wrong hydrogen rule. Correctness, claims, verification and the median are all 2.
